assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational and consequential body of political-economy research linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson and Tabellini are central, identifiable contributors to the modern analytical and empirical political-economy program.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped research across political economy and development for decades and has accumulated broad application.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several connected themes rather than a single sharply bounded discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has transformed the measurement and understanding of intergenerational mobility and its geographic determinants.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are especially closely associated with the core mobility program, with Friedman an important collaborator.
assessment.maturity: The findings are highly influential, extensively developed and consequential for public debate as well as scholarship.
uncertainties: The appropriate attribution boundary among a large collaborative research network is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy analysis of trade policy supplied durable explanations for how organized interests and political incentives shape protection.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman form a clear and compact attribution for the central contribution.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and remains a central reference point in international political economy.
uncertainties: Its empirical reach and institutional assumptions vary across political settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research powerfully redirected attention to legal institutions, investor protection and comparative financial development.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes and Shleifer are central authors of the defining comparative work.
assessment.maturity: The research is mature, widely tested and has influenced both finance and institutional economics.
uncertainties: Causal interpretation of legal-origin patterns has been debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction and interpretation of long-run income, wealth and offshore-wealth distributions have reshaped inequality research.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman are highly visible and central contributors to the linked measurement agenda.
assessment.maturity: The empirical infrastructure and research program are substantial and influential, though still actively developing.
uncertainties: Some wealth and offshore-asset estimates necessarily rely on difficult measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs have made discrimination measurable in compelling field settings and influenced labour-market research and policy.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are particularly closely associated with landmark evidence using these methods.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated, extended and integrated into a broad empirical literature.
uncertainties: Audit-study estimates can depend on the specific market, treatment signal and outcome measured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on teacher quality, accountability and educational production has clarified major mechanisms through which schooling affects life outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Hanushek, Kane and Woessmann each made distinctive, major contributions to the stated research area.
assessment.maturity: The work is mature and has generated extensive evaluation evidence across education systems.
uncertainties: Policy effects are context-dependent, and the contribution is diffuse across several large literatures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work brought rigorous economic analysis to exhaustible resources, biodiversity and the sustainability of wealth.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal provide a clear pairing for foundational contributions to this field.
assessment.maturity: The intellectual contribution is long standing and increasingly relevant to policy, with a durable theoretical base.
uncertainties: Valuing biodiversity and inclusive wealth remains empirically and conceptually challenging.
